subplans.title: The Unknown Bacterium: Discovery and Biology
Surveillance, Case Counts, and Disputed Cause

genre_note: Single-document science/health cluster (Yahoo News syndication of an NBC News report on the 2023 mysterious canine respiratory illness). The document is topically unified but has four clearly separable sub-topics, so it splits on coherence, not size: (a) the UNH sequencing discovery and the biology of the unnamed bacterium, (b) government/state surveillance and case counts, (c) the contested causal attribution, and (d) symptom recognition plus owner advice. Building-block distribution matches the news genre: empirical_observation and concept dominate (dated findings, agency statements, state case tallies, entity descriptions of the illness and the bacterium). One genuine model note exists — Jandrey's causal chain from small pathogen size to evasion of upper-respiratory defenses to pneumonia. One argument (no diagnostic test plus symptom overlap with canine influenza and Bordetella, therefore the true case count likely runs to thousands) and one counter_argument (negative viral testing, Parrish's claim that a viral signature would have surfaced in days, and the caveat that the UNH result still needs confirmation) are both explicitly grounded in the text. procedure is unusually well-attested for a news piece because roughly a third of the article is step-shaped advisory content from the AKC chief veterinarian and from the Oregon State lab director. No hypothesis note was produced — the only forward-looking sentence is a confirmation caveat on an existing finding, which belongs with the counter_argument rather than being inflated into a testable prediction. Absence of hypothesis is a finding, not a gap. Two entity-shaped subjects (the illness itself, the bacterium) are each held by exactly one note so that evidence is not split across near-duplicates; since the cluster has only one document, no cross-document block sharing was needed.
